Get off at the second stop and go along the avenue.
Excuse me. Is there a subway station near here?
Sure. Go along this avenue for three blocks.
Three blocks. And then?
At the third corner there is a crosswalk. Cross there. The entrance is on the other side.
Thank you. How much is the fare?
Three dollars, and it is the same to any station.
I need the green line. Do I pay again for the transfer?
No. You change at Union Square and it costs nothing.
Perfect. How long does it take at this time?
Twenty minutes. But it is rush hour, so give yourself thirty.
Thirty. That is still better than my commute at home. Thank you.
Excuse me, where is the nearest subway station?
How much is the fare to downtown?
Does this train go to Union Square?
Where do I make the transfer?
It is three blocks from here, on the left.

Good morning and welcome aboard. This is a downtown express train. The next stop is Union Square, where you can make a transfer to the green line at no extra cost. Please stand back from the edge of the platform while the doors are closing. During rush hour we run one train every three minutes, so do not run for this one. The fare gates at Union Square are on the upper level, next to the exit. Thank you for riding with us.

Of course, I can help you find it. Turn right when you leave the hotel and walk along this avenue for three blocks. You will pass a small park on your left. At the third corner there is a crosswalk. Cross there, and the subway entrance is on the other side, between a coffee shop and a bank. It is about eight minutes on foot, but at rush hour the sidewalk is slow, so give yourself twelve.

First, Thiago leaves the hotel and walks three blocks along the avenue. Then he crosses at the crosswalk and goes down to the subway. After that, he pays the fare and waits on the platform. Next, he makes a transfer to the green line at Union Square. Finally, he gets off two stops later and walks across the park to the office.
